findings.description: The spec delta adds 'Router value wins when the router is reachable' and 'agents.yaml supplies the value when the router is silent' as delivered requirements, but no production code exercises the router rung: resolve_isolation(router_reachable=True, ...) is only ever called from tests, and the actual dispatch layer (_build_options) hardcodes isolation='worktree' for write phases without consulting the router's assignment.isolation or get_agent_isolation(). Design D3 explicitly defers execution wiring to dg-06, so this is intentional, but the vendor-dispatch spec as written promises behavior this change does not wire. Recommend annotating the spec/tasks that the ladder's router rung is a helper contract whose production caller lands in dg-06, so the archived spec does not overclaim.
findings.resolution: Add a scoping note to the precedence-ladder requirement (or its scenarios) stating the router rung is wired by dg-06; keep the helper as-is.

findings.description: IsolationContractError subclasses ValueError, so an invalid present isolation value in agents.yaml (e.g. 'container') raised by local_static_route is swallowed here into a warning plus None ('no decision'). The caller then proceeds with its own static posture, which is exactly the 'silently substituted posture' the spec's 'An unrecognized isolation value is rejected' scenario forbids. The contract module fails loud, but the only production consumer of the fallback demotes that to a log line.
findings.resolution: Re-raise contract errors (or map them to a distinct hard failure) instead of folding them into the generic ValueError branch; e.g. catch routing_fallback's contract error type first and propagate.

findings.description: The test name claims parity with the reachable router, but it only runs local_static_route. The spec scenario 'Router and local fallback agree on a configured mode override' requires both paths to emit the same value for the same agents.yaml; today that is asserted by two independent tests with separately hand-written fixtures (test_resolver.py builds a lane dict by hand, this test writes YAML). A drift in VendorRegistryService._isolation_by_dispatch_mode versus configured_isolation_value would not be caught by either.
findings.resolution: Either rename the test to describe what it checks, or add a true parity test that loads one agents.yaml through VendorRegistryService._lane -> build_feasible_assignments and through local_static_route and asserts equal assignment.isolation per dispatch mode.

findings.description: _isolation_contract re-executes isolation_contract.py on every call and is invoked from both load_routing_policy_document and local_static_route, so each fallback route execs the module at least twice and registers a fresh sys.modules entry per distinct path (tests with tmp_path accumulate entries). It also yields an IsolationContractError class distinct from src.isolation_contract's, so callers cannot catch the coordinator's exception type across the boundary. Behaviorally fine, but cheap to memoize per resolved path.
findings.resolution: Cache the loaded module keyed by resolved path (e.g. functools.lru_cache on a helper taking the Path) and pass it through rather than reloading.

findings.description: Two scenario headings (lines 52 and 80) directly follow the previous scenario's last line with no blank line, unlike every other scenario in the file. Markdown renderers tolerate it, but it is inconsistent with the rest of the spec and with how openspec-generated deltas are formatted.
findings.resolution: Insert a blank line before the '#### Scenario' headings at lines 52 and 80.

findings.description: ModeConfig.isolation in the review dispatcher is parsed as a bare str and never validated against the canonical vocabulary or consumed. That matches task 2.2's 'parse the additive field' scope, but note this is a consumer-side carrier that does not yet reference the shared definition; when dg-06 wires it, it should validate via the contract rather than trusting the dispatch-config payload.
findings.resolution: No change now; track for dg-06.
